extract_contents.description: Read one or more web pages and get them back as clean markdown: either the passages that matter for your objective, or the whole page.

excerpts: The entry tier bills at $0.034 per...
results.title: Managed Postgres pricing, compared

extract_contents.name: extract_contents

parameters.description: The web addresses (URLs) of the pages to read, such as those from an earlier search. Up to 20 at a time. Pass a list even when there is only one page.
parameters.name: urls

parameters.description: What you want out of these pages, so Parallel can pick the passages that matter. Leave blank to get a general read of each page.
parameters.name: objective

parameters.description: Optional short keyword queries used alongside the objective to pick which passages of each page are worth returning.
parameters.name: search_queries

parameters.description: Return each page in full instead of just the relevant passages. Leave off unless a later step needs the entire page; excerpts are usually enough and far shorter.
parameters.name: full_content

parameters.description: Trim each page to roughly this many characters. Leave blank to let Parallel decide.
parameters.name: max_chars_per_result

error_count.description: How many pages could not be read.

errors.description: The pages that could not be read, and why.

results.description: One entry per page that could be read, with its excerpts and, when requested, its full content.

session_id.description: Session ID tying related searches and page reads together.

get_research_task.description: Check a research task by its run ID and get the result once it has finished. Use this to collect a long Pro or Ultra run that outlasted the wait on 'Run a research task'.
get_research_task.name: get_research_task

parameters.description: The research run's ID, as returned by 'Run a research task', for example, 'trun_9f2c1b4e6a7d4f8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d'.
parameters.name: run_id

basis.description: Parallel's reasoning and confidence for each field of the output.

citation_count.description: How many sources the answer cites.

completed.description: Whether the research finished and an output is included.

output.description: The researched answer, once the run has completed.

run_id.description: Parallel's ID for this research run.

status.description: The run's status: queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled, or action_required.

run_research_task.description: Hand Parallel a research question and get back a researched answer with citations, reasoning, and per-field confidence. Parallel plans the search, reads the sources, and returns structured output.

basis.reasoning: Compared the published price pages for each provider.

excerpts: The entry tier bills at $0.034 per...
citations.title: Managed Postgres pricing, compared

mock_response.output: Managed Postgres entry pricing lands between $0.03 and $0.05 per vCPU-hour across the major providers.

run_research_task.name: run_research_task

parameters.description: What to research, written as a self-contained request, for example, 'Summarize how each major cloud provider prices managed Postgres, and note the cheapest entry tier'.
parameters.name: objective

parameters.description: How much research to do. 'Base' suits most questions. The higher tiers read more sources and reason further but take much longer; a Pro or Ultra run often outlasts the wait below, in which case this step hands back a run ID to collect later.
parameters.name: processor

parameters.description: Plain-language description of what the answer should contain, for example 'A one-paragraph summary plus a list of providers with their entry price'. Leave blank to let Parallel choose the shape. A JSON Schema can be pasted here instead to pin the exact fields.
parameters.name: output_schema

parameters.description: Only use sources from these websites (for example, sec.gov or nytimes.com). A bare extension such as .edu or .gov also works. Leave blank to search the whole web.
parameters.name: include_domains

parameters.description: Leave out sources from these websites (for example, reddit.com or pinterest.com).
parameters.name: exclude_domains

parameters.description: Only use pages published on or after this date, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Useful for keeping research to recent sources.
parameters.name: after_date

parameters.description: How long this step waits for the research to finish, in seconds (default 300, maximum 900). If the run is still going when the wait runs out, the step succeeds and returns its run ID, so use 'Check a research task' later to collect the result.
parameters.name: max_wait_seconds

basis.description: Parallel's reasoning and confidence for each field of the output.

citation_count.description: How many sources the answer cites.

citations.description: The sources behind the answer, each with its web address and the output field it supports.

completed.description: Whether the research finished and an output is included.

output.description: The researched answer: text when no shape was requested, otherwise a structured object.

processor.description: The processor tier the run used.

run_id.description: Parallel's ID for this research run. Pass it to 'Check a research task' to collect a result later.

status.description: The run's status: queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled, or action_required.

timed_out.description: True when the wait ran out before the research finished. The run keeps going on Parallel's side.

search_web.description: Search the web with Parallel and get ranked pages with long, relevant excerpts already pulled out of each one.
search_web.display_str_template: Search the web with Parallel for {0}.

excerpts: Managed Postgres starts at $0.034 per vCPU-hour...
results.title: Managed Postgres pricing, compared

search_web.name: search_web

parameters.description: Short keyword queries, 3-6 words each. Two or three give the best results, for example, 'managed Postgres pricing' and 'cloud database price per hour'.
parameters.name: search_queries

parameters.description: What you are trying to find out, written as a self-contained sentence or two, for example, 'Find the latest published pricing for each major cloud provider's managed Postgres offering'. Parallel uses this to judge which parts of each page matter.
parameters.name: objective

parameters.description: How much work Parallel puts into the search. 'Advanced' is the best quality and the default; 'Basic' is quicker and works well with two or three sharp queries; 'Turbo' is the fastest.
parameters.name: mode

parameters.description: How many pages to return, up to 40. Defaults to 10.
parameters.name: max_results

parameters.description: Only use sources from these websites (for example, sec.gov or nytimes.com). A bare extension such as .edu or .gov also works. Leave blank to search the whole web.
parameters.name: include_domains

parameters.description: Leave out sources from these websites (for example, reddit.com or pinterest.com).
parameters.name: exclude_domains

parameters.description: Only use pages published on or after this date, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Useful for keeping research to recent sources.
parameters.name: after_date

parameters.description: Trim each page's excerpts to roughly this many characters. Leave blank to let Parallel decide.
parameters.name: max_chars_per_result

results.description: The matching pages, most relevant first, each with its web address, title, publish date, and excerpts.

session_id.description: Session ID tying related searches and page reads together.

description: Search the web, read pages as clean markdown, and run deep web research that comes back with citations and confidence levels, using Parallel's APIs built for AI agents.
